title: Least tensor-supporting submodule for a flat Mittag-Leffler module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ a flat Mittag-Leffler $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-trf-mittag-leffler-module]. For every $R$-module $E$ and every $x\in E\otimes_R M$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], there exists a smallest submodule $E_0\subseteq E$ such that $x$ belongs to the image of $E_0\otimes_R M\to E\otimes_R M$ induced by inclusion; moreover this smallest submodule $E_0$ is a finite $R$-module.

proof.text: For each submodule $N\subseteq E$, write $i_N:N\hookrightarrow E$ and $T_N=i_N\otimes\mathrm{id}_M$. By flatness [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $T_N$ is injective. Let $I$ be the set of submodules $N$ for which $x\in\operatorname{im}T_N$; it is a set, being a subset of the power set of $E$, and is nonempty since $E\in I$ and $T_E$ is the identity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Put $K=\bigcap_{N\in I}N$, $P=\prod_{N\in I}E/N$, and define the linear map $q:E\to P$ by $q(e)=(e+N)_{N\in I}$. For each $e\in E$, $q(e)=0$ if and only if $e\in N$ for every $N\in I$. Hence $\ker q=K$, so $0\to K\xrightarrow{i_K}E\xrightarrow{q}P$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 0AS6 (lemma-minimal-contains), first paragraph and the quotient-product map

proof.text: Define $\beta:P\otimes_R M\to\prod_{N\in I}((E/N)\otimes_R M)$ by $\beta((a_N)_N\otimes m)=(a_N\otimes m)_N$, using the bilinear universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The factor swaps $A\otimes_R M\to M\otimes_R A$, $a\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes a$, are well-defined linear maps by that same property; swapping again is the identity on pure tensors and hence on the whole module. With these swaps on its source and each target component, $\beta$ is the map $\theta_{M,(E/N)}$ of [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module]: the formulas agree on every pure tensor. That definition and the Mittag-Leffler hypothesis make $\theta_{M,(E/N)}$ injective, so $\beta$ is injective as well. The index $I$ is a set and each quotient is an $R$-module, exactly the hypotheses of the definition.

source.place: Tag 0AS6 (lemma-minimal-contains), use of Proposition Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), condition (2)

proof.text: For $N\in I$ choose a lift $y_N\in N\otimes_R M$ with $T_N(y_N)=x$. Let $q_N:E\to E/N$ be the quotient map. Since $q_Ni_N=0$, functoriality and the zero-map identity in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] give $(q_N\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(x)=0$. The $N$th component of $\beta((q\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(x))$ equals $(q_N\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(x)$: on $e\otimes m$ both are $(e+N)\otimes m$, and pure tensors generate. Thus every component is zero. Injectivity of $\beta$ from Step 2 gives $(q\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(x)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AS6 (lemma-minimal-contains), the two displayed quotient-product maps

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to the exact sequence $0\to K\xrightarrow{i_K}E\xrightarrow{q}P$ of Step 1, with the given flat module $M$. It gives $\ker(q\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)=\operatorname{im}(i_K\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)$. Step 3 therefore provides $y\in K\otimes_R M$ mapping to $x$. In particular $K\in I$. By its definition as the intersection, $K\subseteq N$ for every $N\in I$. Consequently $K$ is the least supporting submodule. This application uses exactness at $E$, with the zero left endpoint; it makes no assumption that $q$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0AS6 (lemma-minimal-contains), kernel identification; Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), exactness of tensoring by a flat module

proof.text: By the pure-tensor generation in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], the lift $y$ is a finite sum $y=\sum_{j=1}^r f_j\otimes m_j$ with $f_j\in K$, $m_j\in M$: any scalar coefficient in a finite linear combination can be absorbed into $f_j$ by bilinearity. Let $L\subseteq E$ consist of the linear combinations $\sum_{j=1}^r a_j f_j$ with $a_j\in R$. This is a submodule contained in $K$. The tensor $\sum_j f_j\otimes m_j$, now formed in $L\otimes_R M$, maps to $x$, by the formula for the induced tensor map in the same definition. Hence $L\in I$, and leastness from Step 4 gives $K\subseteq L$. Therefore $K=L$, which is generated by the finite list $f_1,\ldots,f_r$. Taking $E_0=K$ proves the finiteness assertion (finite means finitely generated over $R$).

Statement: it matches 0AS6 hypothesis by hypothesis. M is flat Mittag-Leffler, E is an arbitrary module, there is a least submodule whose tensor image contains x, and that submodule is finite. Nothing is weakened or added. Step 1 (elementary): the set I of supporting submodules contains E, and the kernel of q: E -> prod_{N in I} E/N is the intersection K; checked pointwise, and q is not assumed surjective. Step 2 (elementary): beta is the Mittag-Leffler map theta_{M,(E/N)} of def-trf-mittag-leffler-module conjugated by the factor swaps, checked on pure tensors; that definition covers families indexed by any set, so I is allowed. Step 3 (elementary): (q_N tensor 1)(x)=0 follows from the composition and zero-map clauses of the tensor-product node; the components of beta then show (q tensor 1)(x)=0, which is Stacks' use of 059M. Step 4: the first sentence of the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact applied to K->E->P gives x in the image of K tensor M, so K is the least support. Step 5 (elementary): the coefficients f_j of one lift span a submodule L contained in K that is itself a support, so K=L is finitely generated. proof_deps equals the union of the uses. No new nodes. No cycle (the item does not cite its parent). No off-unit route: the only non-definition dependency is a Mathlib leaf, so no tool_uses are needed and none were accepted. No SGA citation. No base-change morphism or coefficient category is involved (commutative algebra, not a target node). Duplicates: rg over dag/nodes for 0AS6, minimal-contains, smallest/least submodule and Mittag finds no other node stating this. The parent is the finite-free criterion and uses this item for its forward direction, so the item is not a restated clause. Small cases: x=0, E=0 or M=0 give K=0. M=R gives K=Re. Over a field with x = sum e_j tensor b_j (b_j a basis), K is the span of the e_j. R=Z, M=Q, x=1 tensor 1 in Z tensor Q: every nZ is a support but the intersection 0 is not, so the Mittag-Leffler hypothesis is really used. Minor, no change: the report mentions citations.json and searches.jsonl, which are not on the branch. No fixes written; review.md is in the run directory.
